attention: block-causal in the 6 full-attention layers: the input is cut into [start, stop) blocks of at most block_size tokens (state blocks; one short question block, or catalogue blocks + rubric blocks when question + options + slots exceed block_size); every block attends to all earlier tokens and to itself with no causal mask inside the block. Gated-DeltaNet layers are ordinary recurrent layers.
score: per option k: logit[' yes'] - logit[' no'] at the k-th ' ->' slot, computed as h_slot . (w_yes - w_no) from the final normed hidden state and the tied embedding rows (float32)
probabilities: softmax(scores / T) in canonical option order; T = temperatures.by_qtype[question type] (choice / noul / score), fitted on held-out calibration rows

images.placeholder: <|image_k|> in the state (k = 1..n, each exactly once) becomes <|vision_start|> + n_tokens x <|image_pad|> + <|vision_end|>; a state without placeholders gets {"image": "<|image_1|>", ...} (several: image_1..image_n) added first, as in the training data
images.resolution: native, capped at max_pixels (default 1,638,400 = 1.6 MP, LANCZOS downscale, aspect kept), then sized to multiples of 32 px (patch 16 x merge 2); one image token per 32 x 32 px
images.encoder: the checkpoint's own Qwen3.5 vision tower and image processor (preprocessor_config.json)

budgets.note: the complete input (state incl. image tokens + question + options + readout) <= max_len tokens; there is no separate question/options cap; larger inputs raise InputBudgetError, nothing is truncated

temperatures.fitted_on: 3,325 held-out calibration rows (not training, not dev rows)
temperatures.selection: per-question-type temperatures are used because they lowered the two-fold held-out NLL (0.2470 global -> 0.2459 per type)
temperatures.selected_weights: uniform average of the final weights of two training runs (seeds 0 and 1)
